panels.title: Edge Protection Coverage
panels.description: Reads the last `edge-audit` skill verdict for $overlay (edge-audit SKILL.md Step 4b). This is a POINT-IN-TIME audit result, not a live WAF-hit stream — see the heartbeat panel below for staleness.

panels.title: Last Audit Age
panels.description: Thresholds match the {@ service_slug @}EdgeAuditHeartbeatMissing alert (7d warn, 14d fires).

panels.title: Requests Reaching Origin
panels.description: Traffic that made it PAST the edge layer to the origin — the same metric the Inference dashboard's Request Rate panel shows. A sudden drop here with no corresponding drop in the native WAF console's traffic view can indicate an edge misconfiguration blocking legitimate traffic.

panels.title: Deep WAF / DDoS Analytics — use the native console

options.content:
This template deliberately does **not** duplicate per-rule hit counts, bot scores, or DDoS-attack timelines in Grafana — Cloud Armor, AWS WAFv2, and Cloudflare each already ship a purpose-built analytics view for exactly this, and re-implementing it here would drift out of sync with each provider's own rule taxonomy (see `docs/observability/monitoring-stations.md`, Engineering Calibration Principle). Use:

- **Cloud Armor**: GCP Console → Network Security → Cloud Armor policies → `<service>-edge-policy` → Monitoring tab
- **AWS WAFv2**: AWS Console → WAF & Shield → Web ACLs → `<service>-edge-acl` → Sampled requests / CloudWatch metrics
- **Cloudflare**: Dashboard → your zone → Security → Events

What this dashboard DOES track — coverage (is a WAF wired in at all) and audit freshness — is the piece those consoles cannot answer, since none of them know this template's D-38 contract.
